title: Completed normalization model and branch geometry of a nodal curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C$ be a nonempty proper reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension], smooth except at nodes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], meaning that each nonsmooth point $x$ has completed local ring $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $
u:\widetilde C	o C$ be its reduced normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] and $S$ its nonsmooth locus. Then $C$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally covered by spectra of Noetherian rings) [pqf-def-locnoeth], $S$ is a finite set of closed $k$-points, and $
u$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. There are finitely many smooth projective connected components $C_a$ of $\widetilde C$, and $
u$ is an isomorphism over $C\setminus S$. For each $x\in S$, let $(A,\mathfrak m)=\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and let $Q(A)$ be the localization obtained by inverting all non-zero-divisors. The integral closure $B\subset Q(A)$ of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is canonically $(
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde C})_x$, is finite over $A$, and has exactly two maximal ideals, both with residue field $k$, corresponding to the two points of $
u^{-1}(x)$. The local ring $A$ has dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For any chosen nodal presentation of $\widehat A$, its normalization is $P=k[[u]]	imes k[[v]]$ with $\widehat A\hookrightarrow P$ given by $h\mapsto(h(u,0),h(0,v))$. Its image consists exactly of pairs with equal constant terms, and $Q(\widehat A)=k((u))	imes k((v))$, where $k((t))$ denotes Laurent series with finitely many negative powers. The canonical maps identify $B\otimes_A\widehat A=\varprojlim_n B/\mathfrak m^nB$ with $P$ as $\widehat A$-algebras [def-weil-module-base-change]; the two residue maps from $B$ are the restrictions of the two constant-term maps on $P$. Consequently the inverse images of $S$ and of any finite set of smooth closed points form a finite set on each $C_a$.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), normalization setup and completed replacement of its branch-ring calculation; varieties.tex Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion); algebra.tex Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain).

proof.text: Properness includes finite type and separatedness. The spectrum of the field $k$ is Noetherian: its coordinate ring has just the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$. Therefore lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian makes $C$ Noetherian, including quasi-compactness. By lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components its reduced irreducible components form a finite family $Z_a$. Each has dimension one by the pure-dimension hypothesis. We use precisely their disjoint union of function-field normalizations, as prescribed by def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization.

Apply lem-trf-normalization-singular-skyscraper to $C$: the field is algebraically closed, $C$ is reduced and finite type, and all its irreducible components have dimension one. Its nonsmooth locus is the set $S$ in the question, hence is finite and consists of closed points with residue field $k$. The same statement gives finiteness of $\nu$ and identifies $(\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde C})_x$ with the integral closure of $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$ in $Q(A)$. Denote this canonical algebra by $B$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), parts (1)--(4), and finite-type perfect-field specialization

proof.text: For each reduced component $Z_a$, its closed inclusion in proper $C$ makes $Z_a$ proper, by the closed-immersion and composition clauses of lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence. It is integral, finite type, and of dimension one. Apply lem-sc-normalization-properties: $C_a=Z_a^\nu$ is integral, proper, of dimension one, and smooth since the algebraically closed field is perfect (in characteristic $p>0$, every $a\in k$ has a $p$-th root because $T^p-a$ splits). Apply lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective to conclude that $C_a$ is projective. An integral nonempty scheme is connected, so these finitely many disjoint summands are exactly the connected components of $\widetilde C$.

Since $S$ is a finite set of closed points, $U=C\setminus S$ is open. It is a smooth curve by definition of $S$, so its local rings are normal by lem-sc-smooth-normal. The restriction clause (2) of lem-per-componentwise-normalization-properties applies to the locally Noetherian scheme $C$ and its normal open $U$, and gives $\nu^{-1}(U)\simeq U$ over $U$.

Fix $x\in S$. By lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains, $\dim A$ is the supremum of the lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets starting at $\{x\}$. Every such chain lies in an irreducible component of $C$, of dimension one, so has length at most one. A component containing $x$ has dimension one and thus is not $\{x\}$; the chain $\{x\}\subsetneq Z_a$ has length one. Thus $\dim A=1$. The ring $A$ is reduced by def-pc-reduced-scheme. Choose a Noetherian affine neighbourhood; its localization at $x$ is Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian. An affine finite-type neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}T$ identifies $A$ with $T_{\mathfrak p_x}$, so $A$ is essentially of finite type over $k$ in the explicit localization sense of def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra.

Apply lem-trf-curve-normalization-completion to this reduced, one-dimensional local algebra essentially of finite type over $k$. It states that $B$ is finite over $A$ and that $B\otimes_A\widehat A$ is canonically the integral closure of $\widehat A$ in $Q(\widehat A)$, with the structural embedding extending $A\to\widehat A$. In particular this step uses the finite-type hypothesis: it does not assert normalization commutes with completion for arbitrary Noetherian local rings.

Write $R=k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ using the chosen nodal presentation. A series has a unique expression modulo $(uv)$ of the form $c+u f(u)+v g(v)$: its mixed monomials form $uv$ times the series obtained by lowering both exponents by one. The coefficientwise map $h\mapsto(h(u,0),h(0,v))$ has kernel exactly $(uv)$. It therefore embeds $R$ in $P=k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$, with image precisely the pairs $(f,g)$ satisfying $f(0)=g(0)$. For such a pair the inverse is represented by $f(u)+g(v)-f(0)$. These identities follow directly from the coefficient definition of formal power series.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, Case I; explicit coefficient calculation

proof.text: In this equal-constant subring a pair is a non-zero-divisor exactly when both its coordinates are nonzero: use that each one-variable series ring is a domain; if a coordinate is zero, multiplication by the nonzero element $(u,0)$ or $(0,v)$ in the opposite coordinate kills the pair. Thus localization embeds $Q(R)$ in $k((u))\times k((v))$, since the Laurent series rings are fields. For any Laurent pair $(F,G)$ choose $N>0$ large enough that $u^NF$ and $v^NG$ have strictly positive order (zero coordinates cause no restriction). Both $(u^NF,v^NG)$ and the denominator $(u^N,v^N)$ belong to $R$, and the denominator is a non-zero-divisor. Their quotient is $(F,G)$. Hence $Q(R)=k((u))\times k((v))$.

source.place: Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), Laurent series in its proof; explicit localization calculation

proof.text: Inside $Q(R)$ put $e=(1,0)$. For $(f,g)\in P$ set $c=f(0)-g(0)$; then $(f,g)-ce\in R$. Thus $P$ is generated over $R$ by $1,e$, and is integral over $R$ by lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral. Apply lem-weil-pbc-power-series-normal-domain to the Noetherian normal domain $k$: both factors $k[[u]]$ and $k[[v]]$ are integrally closed in their fraction fields. These fraction fields are the indicated Laurent fields, since a Laurent series becomes a power series after multiplication by a power of its variable. If $(F,G)\in Q(R)$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $R$, its coordinate equations are monic equations over the two series rings, whence $F\in k[[u]]$ and $G\in k[[v]]$. This proves that the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$ is exactly $P$, with the specified embedding.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral) and 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain); curves.tex Tag 0C4A Case I

proof.text: Combining steps 6 and 9 identifies $B\otimes_A\widehat A$ with $P$ as $\widehat A$-algebras. Since $A$ is Noetherian and $B$ finite, lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor gives the canonical isomorphism $\widehat A\otimes_A B\simeq\varprojlim_n B/\mathfrak m^n B$; interchange the two tensor factors. The formula is $a\otimes b\mapsto(a_n b\bmod\mathfrak m^n B)_n$, so it preserves multiplication and the unit, not just addition and scalars. We obtain precisely the canonical algebra identifications of the statement; no identification of the uncompleted semilocal ring $B$ with a product of local rings is made.

source.place: Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3), its canonical map and multiplicativity

proof.text: By lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring, $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ is the maximal ideal of $\widehat A$, so in the nodal coordinates it is $(u,v)$. Its extension to $P$ is $u k[[u]]\times v k[[v]]$. Reducing $B\otimes_A\widehat A=P$ modulo this ideal gives the canonical isomorphism $B/\mathfrak mB\simeq P/\mathfrak mP=k\times k$: explicitly the tensor reduction sends $b\otimes a$ to $\bar b\bar a$ and has inverse $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Every maximal ideal of $B$ contains $\mathfrak mB$ by lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical. The ring $k\times k$ has exactly two prime ideals: in a prime quotient one of the complementary idempotents $(1,0),(0,1)$ must vanish, and the other field factor has zero prime ideal. Consequently $B$ has exactly two maximal ideals with residue field $k$, and its two quotient maps are the restrictions of the constant-term maps of $P$.

The two maximal ideals just found give exactly the two points of $\nu^{-1}(x)$. To check this with the actual normalization, take an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}T$ of $x$. By lem-per-componentwise-normalization-affine-charts its inverse image is the spectrum of the product of the integral closures of the minimal-prime quotients of $T$. Localizing this algebra at $T\setminus\mathfrak p_x$ gives its stalk $B$: integral closure commutes with localization by lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization, and the stalk is the integral closure already identified in step 2. The fibre ring is therefore $B\otimes_A k=B/\mathfrak mB$. The prime and residue-field identifications of lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields give exactly the two points and their residue maps computed in step 11, compatibly with the canonical map from $B$.

Finally, a finite morphism has finite fibres by lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres. Thus the inverse image under $\nu$ of the finite set $S$, or of any finite set of smooth closed points, is a finite union of finite sets. Intersecting this set with any component $C_a$ preserves finiteness, proving the last assertion (and covering $S=\varnothing$).
